title: Restriction of modules to an open is left adjoint to the direct image
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and $\mathcal O_X$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $X$, and let $U\subseteq X$ be an open subset. Write $\mathcal O_U=\mathcal O_X|_U$ for the sheaf of rings $W\mapsto\mathcal O_X(W)$ on the open subsets $W\subseteq U$, and for a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal M$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] write $\mathcal M|_U$ for the $\mathcal O_U$-module $W\mapsto\mathcal M(W)$ ($W\subseteq U$ open) with the restriction maps and module structures of $\mathcal M$ [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]; for a morphism $\alpha:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules let $\alpha|_U$ have the components $\alpha_W$, $W\subseteq U$. For a sheaf of $\mathcal O_U$-modules $\mathcal G$ let $j_*\mathcal G$ be the sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $V\mapsto\mathcal G(V\cap U)$ ($V\subseteq X$ open), with the restriction maps of $\mathcal G$ and with $\mathcal O_X(V)$ acting on $\mathcal G(V\cap U)$ through the restriction $\mathcal O_X(V)\to\mathcal O_X(V\cap U)=\mathcal O_U(V\cap U)$; for a morphism $\beta:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ of $\mathcal O_U$-modules let $(j_*\beta)_V=\beta_{V\cap U}$. Then $\mathcal M\mapsto\mathcal M|_U$ and $\mathcal G\mapsto j_*\mathcal G$ are functors $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ and $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, and the first is left adjoint to the second: for all $\mathcal M\in\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ and $\mathcal G\in\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ the map $\Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal M|_U,\mathcal G)\to\Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal M,j_*\mathcal G)$ sending $\alpha$ to the morphism with components $\mathcal M(V)\to\mathcal G(V\cap U)$, $s\mapsto\alpha_{V\cap U}(s|_{V\cap U})$, is a bijection, natural in $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal G$; its inverse sends $\beta$ to the morphism with components $\beta_W:\mathcal M(W)\to(j_*\mathcal G)(W)=\mathcal G(W)$ for $W\subseteq U$ open.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 0096 (sheaves-lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules: f^* is left adjoint to f_* for a morphism of ringed spaces) applied to the inclusion j:(U,O_X|_U)->(X,O_X), with Lemma 00A0 (sheaves-lemma-j-pullback: j^{-1}G is V -> G(V) for V in U, also for sheaves of modules) and Definition 00A1 (sheaves-definition-restriction (3),(4)); for this j, j^*M = O_U (x)_{j^{-1}O_X} j^{-1}M = j^{-1}M = M|_U since j^{-1}O_X = O_U; the pushforward is Definition 0095 (sheaves-definition-pushforward)

proof.text: *Step 1 (restriction is a functor $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$).* Sheaves on $X$ and on $U$ are sheaves on the sites of open subsets with open coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]; the open subsets of $U$ are exactly the open subsets of $X$ contained in $U$. Let $\mathcal M\in\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The rule $W\mapsto\mathcal M(W)$ ($W\subseteq U$ open) with the restriction maps of $\mathcal M$ is a presheaf of abelian groups on $U$ (composition and identity laws are those of $\mathcal M$). A covering $\{W_i\to W\}$ of an open $W\subseteq U$ in the site of $U$ is a family of opens $W_i\subseteq W$ with $\bigcup_iW_i=W$, i.e. a covering of $W$ in the site of $X$, and the sheaf condition for $\mathcal M|_U$ on it is word for word the sheaf condition for $\mathcal M$ on it; so $\mathcal M|_U$ is a sheaf. In the same way $\mathcal O_U$ is a sheaf of rings on $U$. For $W\subseteq U$, $\mathcal M(W)$ is an $\mathcal O_X(W)=\mathcal O_U(W)$-module and for $W'\subseteq W\subseteq U$ the restriction $\mathcal M(W)\to\mathcal M(W')$ is semilinear over $\mathcal O_U(W)\to\mathcal O_U(W')$, which is the restriction of $\mathcal O_X$; so $\mathcal M|_U$ is a sheaf of $\mathcal O_U$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the restriction of [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. For a morphism $\mu:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules the components $\mu_W$, $W\subseteq U$, are $\mathcal O_X(W)=\mathcal O_U(W)$-linear and commute with the restriction maps $W'\subseteq W$, so $\mu|_U$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules; $(\nu\circ\mu)|_U=\nu|_U\circ\mu|_U$ and $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal M}|_U=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal M|_U}$ hold componentwise. Hence $(-)|_U$ is a functor.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 00A0 (label lemma-j-pullback, line 4453), statement (2) and last sentence (modules) with the proof of (2); Definition Tag 00A1 (label definition-restriction, line 4495), (3) and (4)

proof.text: *Step 2 ($j_*$ is a functor $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$).* Let $\mathcal G\in\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ and write $j:U\to X$ for the inclusion, so $j^{-1}(V)=V\cap U$. As a presheaf of abelian groups, $j_*\mathcal G$, $V\mapsto\mathcal G(V\cap U)$, with restriction maps $\mathcal G(V\cap U)\to\mathcal G(V'\cap U)$ for $V'\subseteq V$, is the direct image of the abelian sheaf $\mathcal G$ along the continuous map $j$, hence a sheaf of abelian groups on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (1) (directly: an open covering $V=\bigcup_iV_i$ gives the open covering $V\cap U=\bigcup_i(V_i\cap U)$ in $U$, and the sheaf condition of $j_*\mathcal G$ for the first is that of $\mathcal G$ for the second, with $(V_i\cap U)\cap(V_k\cap U)=(V_i\cap V_k)\cap U$). Module structure: for $V\subseteq X$ open let $\rho_V:\mathcal O_X(V)\to\mathcal O_X(V\cap U)=\mathcal O_U(V\cap U)$ be the restriction, a ring homomorphism; $a\cdot t:=\rho_V(a)t$ for $a\in\mathcal O_X(V)$, $t\in\mathcal G(V\cap U)$ makes $\mathcal G(V\cap U)$ an $\mathcal O_X(V)$-module (restriction of scalars along $\rho_V$), extending its group structure. Semilinearity: for $V'\subseteq V$, $(a\cdot t)|_{V'\cap U}=(\rho_V(a)t)|_{V'\cap U}=\rho_V(a)|_{V'\cap U}\,t|_{V'\cap U}=\rho_{V'}(a|_{V'})\,t|_{V'\cap U}=a|_{V'}\cdot t|_{V'\cap U}$, using the semilinearity of the restriction of $\mathcal G$ and $\rho_V(a)|_{V'\cap U}=a|_{V'\cap U}=\rho_{V'}(a|_{V'})$ (restrictions of $\mathcal O_X$ compose). So $j_*\mathcal G\in\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $\beta:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$, $(j_*\beta)_V=\beta_{V\cap U}$ is additive, commutes with the restriction maps (those of $\mathcal G,\mathcal G'$ along $V'\cap U\subseteq V\cap U$), and is $\mathcal O_X(V)$-linear: $\beta_{V\cap U}(\rho_V(a)t)=\rho_V(a)\beta_{V\cap U}(t)$ by $\mathcal O_U(V\cap U)$-linearity of $\beta_{V\cap U}$. Compositions and identities are preserved componentwise. Two identities used below: for $W\subseteq U$ open, $W\cap U=W$, so $(j_*\mathcal G)(W)=\mathcal G(W)$, $\rho_W=\mathrm{id}$ and the $\mathcal O_X(W)$-module structure of $(j_*\mathcal G)(W)$ is the $\mathcal O_U(W)$-module structure of $\mathcal G(W)$, and for $W'\subseteq W\subseteq U$ the restriction map of $j_*\mathcal G$ is that of $\mathcal G$; and for any open $V\subseteq X$, the restriction map $(j_*\mathcal G)(V)\to(j_*\mathcal G)(V\cap U)$ is the restriction of $\mathcal G$ along $(V\cap U)\cap U=V\cap U$, i.e. the identity of $\mathcal G(V\cap U)$.

proof.text: *Step 3 (the map $\Phi:\alpha\mapsto\beta$).* Let $\mathcal M\in\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, $\mathcal G\in\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ and $\alpha:\mathcal M|_U\to\mathcal G$ a morphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules. For $V\subseteq X$ open define $\beta_V:\mathcal M(V)\to\mathcal G(V\cap U)=(j_*\mathcal G)(V)$, $\beta_V(s)=\alpha_{V\cap U}(s|_{V\cap U})$. It is additive. It is $\mathcal O_X(V)$-linear: for $a\in\mathcal O_X(V)$, $\beta_V(as)=\alpha_{V\cap U}(a|_{V\cap U}s|_{V\cap U})=a|_{V\cap U}\,\alpha_{V\cap U}(s|_{V\cap U})=\rho_V(a)\beta_V(s)=a\cdot\beta_V(s)$, by semilinearity of the restriction of $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal O_U(V\cap U)$-linearity of $\alpha_{V\cap U}$. It commutes with restrictions: for $V'\subseteq V$, $\beta_V(s)|_{V'\cap U}=\alpha_{V\cap U}(s|_{V\cap U})|_{V'\cap U}=\alpha_{V'\cap U}(s|_{V\cap U}|_{V'\cap U})=\alpha_{V'\cap U}((s|_{V'})|_{V'\cap U})=\beta_{V'}(s|_{V'})$, since $\alpha$ commutes with the restriction along $V'\cap U\subseteq V\cap U$ and restrictions of $\mathcal M$ compose. So $\Phi(\alpha):=\beta$ is a morphism $\mathcal M\to j_*\mathcal G$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ (Step 2).

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 0096 (label lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules, line 3157), the bijection, written out for the open inclusion with Lemma Tag 00A0 (j^{-1} = restriction)

proof.text: *Step 4 (the map $\Psi:\beta\mapsto\alpha$).* Let $\beta:\mathcal M\to j_*\mathcal G$ be a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. For $W\subseteq U$ open put $\alpha_W:=\beta_W:\mathcal M(W)=(\mathcal M|_U)(W)\to(j_*\mathcal G)(W)=\mathcal G(W)$ (Step 2). It is additive; it is $\mathcal O_U(W)$-linear, because $\beta_W$ is $\mathcal O_X(W)$-linear, $\mathcal O_X(W)=\mathcal O_U(W)$, and $\mathcal O_X(W)$ acts on $(j_*\mathcal G)(W)$ through $\rho_W=\mathrm{id}$, i.e. by the $\mathcal O_U(W)$-module structure of $\mathcal G(W)$ (Step 2); it commutes with restrictions along $W'\subseteq W\subseteq U$, because $\beta$ does and the restriction maps of $\mathcal M|_U$, resp. $j_*\mathcal G$, on opens of $U$ are those of $\mathcal M$, resp. $\mathcal G$ (Steps 1, 2). So $\Psi(\beta):=\alpha:\mathcal M|_U\to\mathcal G$ is a morphism in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 0096 (label lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules, line 3157), inverse bijection, for the open inclusion; Lemma Tag 00A0 (label lemma-j-pullback), proof of (5): j^{-1}j_*F(V) = j_*F(V) = F(V)

proof.text: *Step 5 ($\Phi$ and $\Psi$ are inverse).* For $\alpha:\mathcal M|_U\to\mathcal G$ and $W\subseteq U$: $\Psi(\Phi(\alpha))_W(s)=\Phi(\alpha)_W(s)=\alpha_{W\cap U}(s|_{W\cap U})=\alpha_W(s|_W)=\alpha_W(s)$, as $W\cap U=W$ and $s|_W=s$. For $\beta:\mathcal M\to j_*\mathcal G$ and $V\subseteq X$ open: $\Phi(\Psi(\beta))_V(s)=\Psi(\beta)_{V\cap U}(s|_{V\cap U})=\beta_{V\cap U}(s|_{V\cap U})$; since $\beta$ commutes with the restriction along $V\cap U\subseteq V$, this equals the image of $\beta_V(s)$ under the restriction map $(j_*\mathcal G)(V)\to(j_*\mathcal G)(V\cap U)$, which is the identity of $\mathcal G(V\cap U)$ (Step 2); so $\Phi(\Psi(\beta))_V(s)=\beta_V(s)$. Hence $\Phi:\Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal M|_U,\mathcal G)\to\Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal M,j_*\mathcal G)$ is a bijection with inverse $\Psi$, which are the maps of the statement.

proof.text:
*Step 6 (naturality, hence the adjunction).* Let $\mu:\mathcal M'	o\mathcal M$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$, $
u:\mathcal G	o\mathcal G'$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ and $\alpha:\mathcal M|_U	o\mathcal G$. Claim: $\Phi(
u\circ\alpha\circ\mu|_U)=j_*
u\circ\Phi(\alpha)\circ\mu$. For $V\subseteq X$ open and $s\in\mathcal M'(V)$: the left side gives $
u_{V\cap U}(\alpha_{V\cap U}(\mu_{V\cap U}(s|_{V\cap U})))$, the right side $(j_*
u)_V(\Phi(\alpha)_V(\mu_V(s)))=
u_{V\cap U}(\alpha_{V\cap U}(\mu_V(s)|_{V\cap U}))$, and $\mu_V(s)|_{V\cap U}=\mu_{V\cap U}(s|_{V\cap U})$ because $\mu$ commutes with restrictions. Taking $
u=\mathrm{id}$, resp. $\mu=\mathrm{id}$, gives naturality of $\Phi$ in $\mathcal M$, resp. in $\mathcal G$ (and $\Psi=\Phi^{-1}$ is then natural too). A family of bijections $\Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal M|_U,\mathcal G)\cong\Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal M,j_*\mathcal G)$ natural in both variables between the functors of Steps 1 and 2 is, by the definition in the statement, an adjunction $(-)|_U\dashv j_*$.
